correctness.rationale: Weighted matrix-tree identity is valid for negative real edge signs as a polynomial identity. Because every three-sign column sum is odd, the Schur elimination is defined. Eight exact rational two-by-two Q matrices are PSD; all with at least two negative signs are PD. Their one-sign null directions are pairwise distinct. Thus M=(n-4|S|)B+sum Q is PD for 4|S|<n, and at n=4|S| singular precisely for distinct-column one-left-vertex stars. Full n=4 tree enumeration and larger exact low-degree searches support, but do not replace, this all-n proof.

value.rationale: The exact smallest vanishing Walsh degree identifies a genuine identifiability threshold for local parity signals of the graphic matroid basis family. It grows linearly with n and is attained only by a structural star motif in the first nontrivial three-left-vertex complete bipartite family. Counts 3 binomial(4q,q) are a complete sharp extremizer census, not a routine small graph computation.
